svg.title: Agent topology and orchestration patterns
svg.desc: Four cards compare Single Agent, Routing, Supervisor and Handoff. The last three are grouped under Multi-Agent. Transparent background with pale rose cards. Single Agent. One agent owns the task from start to finish, selecting and using the skills and tools it needs. Best suited for: Focused business scope, shared context and a manageable set of capabilities. Routing. A routing step classifies the request and selects the relevant specialist agent or agents to handle it. Best suited for: Clear request categories and largely independent specialist tasks. Supervisor. A lead agent breaks down the task, delegates work and coordinates specialists, then combines their results. Best suited for: Cross-domain tasks with dependencies, multiple steps and a unified outcome. Handoff. An agent transfers control and relevant context to another agent, which takes over the task or conversation. Best suited for: Multi-stage journeys that need a change in specialist ownership.
